articles.title: Kenya races to trace all contacts after first Ebola death, WHO official says

events.summary: Kenya has recorded its first Ebola death, triggering a comprehensive contact-tracing effort supported by the United Nations and partner organizations. The World Health Organization's top official in the country confirmed the emergency response.
events.why: A confirmed Ebola fatality in a regional transit hub like Kenya presents serious epidemic risks for East Africa if containment fails.

articles.title: Putin pledges Russia’s support to end US-led war on Iran

events.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin met with the Iranian president in Turkmenistan and pledged Russian support to end the US-led war on Iran. The meeting occurred ahead of a regional summit.
events.why: Direct Russian diplomatic and political intervention in a major US-Iran war significantly impacts regional alliance dynamics and conflict escalation.

articles.title: WHO releases first global guidelines on child obesity as cases surge

events.summary: The World Health Organization has issued its first global guidelines targeting child obesity as rates quadruple since 1990. The condition now affects around eight percent of youth aged five to nineteen, up from two percent.
events.why: Establishing the first global clinical and policy guidelines targets a fast-growing worldwide non-communicable disease burden in youth.

articles.title: At least 81 US aircraft worth up to $3.3bn lost or damaged in Iran war

events.summary: A Congressional Budget Office report states that at least 81 US aircraft worth up to $3.3 billion have been lost or damaged in the war with Iran. The disclosure adds to scrutiny over the financial and military costs of the conflict.
events.why: Substantial US military asset losses impose major financial burdens and reveal notable operational attrition in an ongoing armed conflict.

articles.title: Hegseth says firing squad execution of Fort Hood shooter will be ‘public’
US to livestream Fort Hood shooter's execution: Pentagon
Pentagon says execution of Fort Hood shooter will be livestreamed

events.summary: Pentagon officials announced that the execution by firing squad of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan will be publicly livestreamed. The decision was confirmed by defense leadership.
events.why: Livestreaming a federal military execution sets an extraordinary and controversial legal and media precedent for US capital punishment.

articles.title: Critical funding gap threatens health response in Yemen

events.summary: The World Health Organization warned that a critical funding gap is hindering its capacity to respond to health needs in Yemen. Significantly more resources are required as conflict and humanitarian needs escalate.
events.why: Inadequate funding for humanitarian healthcare in Yemen directly risks lives amid a protracted conflict.

articles.title: Most UK diplomats to leave East Jerusalem consulate, Israel says, as Miliband says 'vital services' to remain
Israel shuts down British consulate in occupied East Jerusalem
Israel’s downgrading of UK consulate aims to tighten its hold on Jerusalem
British consulate in East Jerusalem will stay open as UK mission, says Ed Miliband

events.summary: Israel is forcing most UK diplomats to depart their East Jerusalem consulate following British sanctions on West Bank settlements. UK officials stated that vital diplomatic services will remain operational despite the downgrade.
events.why: The diplomatic expulsion escalates bilateral tensions and affects consular support and political presence in occupied East Jerusalem.

articles.title: Bear kills man in home attack near Mongolian capital

events.summary: A bear entered a traditional nomadic dwelling near Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, killing a man and severely injuring a woman.
events.why: A fatal wildlife encounter is an isolated local incident with minimal societal consequence.
